board: The plan leaves the chat as a GitHub issue written like a PRD, by the `to-prd` skill. The issue outlives the conversation, and the GitHub Projects board over it is where work is tracked. Every issue gets an assignee when it is created.
build: Code and documents are written straight on `main`: no feature branches, no pull requests. A session that writes files works in its own worktree. The module's drawing and its bible section are written in the same pass, every box claimed by one sentence.
capture: What settles is written where the next session will read it: a term in `CONTEXT.md`, a trade-off on its issue or as a proposed ADR, an invariant in its bible chapter. **Watch out:** a new markdown file needs a yes first, and `md_guard` blocks one without it.
check: The person takes the shipped thing in hand and reads the module's drawing to see whether it says what the code does. The tests answer whether it broke; the person answers whether it is right.
decision: The person decides. Facts are looked up, never asked; what reaches the person is judgment, taste, priority and risk, one question at a time. What building teaches comes back here as a question rather than a silent choice.
deleted: Whatever the new work replaces comes out in the commit that adds it. Dead code is a defect, not an archive: a module exists only while deleting it would scatter real complexity across its callers.
dump: Every turn arrives here whichever way it came in: the thought as it comes, with pasted conversations, screenshots and links, no template. A page of thinking rather than a task goes through `/brain-dump` first, and an effort too big for one session goes to `/wayfinder`.
live: Pushing to `main` is the deploy: CronJob `deploy-cycle` every two minutes, and the push receiver at once, run `infra/auto-deploy/auto-deploy.sh` in the cluster, which ships the newest commit the verifying lane (CronJob `commit-gate`) trusts, rebuilds only the images that changed and checks that they roll out. The commit's GitHub page shows `vm/gate`, `vm/build`, `vm/boot` and `vm/deploy`.
orient: Before answering, the assistant reads the repository: the glossary in `CONTEXT.md`, the bible chapters that apply, the area overlays, the decision records and prior issues. The `grill` skill forces those reads, because a session remembers nothing of the last one.
spark: A turn starts because someone wants something that is not there yet, or wants what already runs changed. Nothing has to be broken, and no ticket exists first: the issue is written later in the turn.
verify: Before the push a commit meets the pre-commit hook (torn commits, the test register and its break replay) and the `audit-*` skills. After the push the deploy gate on the server tests the commit in its own tree. A red ships nothing and sends the turn back to building.
watch: The assistant on Signal watches production around the clock: Alertmanager hands it every alert, it decides what reaches a phone, and it writes a weekday brief. What it catches comes back as the next messy prompt.
